source: arXiv:2606.31270 — Learning from Failure: Inference-Time Self-Improvement for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Structured natural-language reflections appended to the agent context on each failed attempt enable materially different choices on retry. Verifiable CI/test outcomes act as the gate for each retry decision.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — AgentForge routes all implementation failures to AIBlocked with no retry; this paper provides the principled pattern for structured reflection + CI-gated autonomous retry in the remediation loop.

source: karpathy/autoresearch — AutoResearch autonomous ML research loop
summary: Minimal 3-file architecture where a Claude agent modifies training code, runs experiments, and uses CI pass/fail as the sole verification gate; discovered 20 optimizations across 700 autonomous experiments.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — AutoResearch's CI-as-verification-gate design is directly analogous to AgentForge's implement→CI→remediation loop; inspired the HID-174 keep-or-discard retry pattern.

source: AAMC — Adaptive Agentic Meta-Controller (ScienceDirect 2026)
summary: Deep RL controller that learns a routing policy across heterogeneous LLMs, selecting which model to invoke per request based on complexity signals and historical success rates.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — AgentForge's agentModels.ts has static tier assignment; AAMC provides the architecture for runtime complexity-based routing that would cut costs 87% in production.

source: Zylos Research — AI Agent Cost Optimization: Token Economics (April 2026)
summary: Documents that 90%/10% model routing (cheap/frontier) achieves 87% cost reduction; identifies issue complexity signals (description length, file scope, failure rate) as sufficient routing features.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — AgentSkill table already tracks failure rates; this study provides the routing thresholds and signal selection for HID-175.

source: Zylos Research — Graceful Degradation Patterns in AI Agent Systems (February 2026)
summary: Documents 41–86.7% production failure rate without deliberate fault tolerance; validates layered fallback chain (retry + alternative runtime) and circuit breaker patterns for agent systems.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — ProcessRunner has no retry; AIBlocked on first process failure; this study directly inspired HID-176 subprocess retry + fallback chain.

source: Vestige — Local-first cognitive memory MCP server with FSRS-6 decay
summary: Local-first MCP server implementing FSRS-6 spaced-repetition decay, spreading activation, contradiction inspection, and active suppression for coding agent memory.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge has zero cross-run memory; Vestige could provide episodic history to subprocess agents. Not selected this run due to lower feasibility score vs. top 3.

source: Mem0 — State of AI Agent Memory Benchmark 2026
summary: Three-layer memory stack benchmark: vector memory for fuzzy recall, episodic buffer for session coherence, graph layer for entity queries; reflection as standard consolidation mechanism.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Natural episode boundaries already exist in the issue state machine; compressed episode summaries post-Done would enable cross-run learning.

source: Zylos Research — AI Agent Memory Architectures: Persistent Knowledge (April 2026)
summary: Frames procedural memory (learned how-to patterns) as the most underexplored memory type for coding agents, distinct from episodic and semantic memory.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Plan and implement stages produce reusable patterns capturable as procedural memory; not selected due to higher integration complexity vs. top 3.

source: arXiv:2510.04371 — Speculative Actions: A Lossless Framework for Faster Agentic Systems
summary: Fast draft model pre-executes predicted next tool calls in parallel; 55% prediction accuracy yields 1.8x–3.7x wall-clock speedup with lossless rollback guarantee.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge is fully sequential; speculative execution would reduce plan-stage latency but requires significant parallelism infrastructure not yet present.

source: LangGraph 1.0 — DeltaChannel, ContextHubBackend, Streaming API v3
summary: LangGraph 1.0 GA adds delta-only checkpointing (store deltas not full state), per-node timeouts with error recovery, and typed streaming channel projections.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — DeltaChannel's delta-store pattern and per-node timeout+recovery are directly applicable to AgentForge's state machine; not selected as no direct LangGraph dependency.

source: Lilian Weng — Harness Engineering for Self-Improvement (July 2026)
summary: Synthesis of patterns for engineering agent harnesses that enable self-improvement; key insight: tight, structured, machine-parseable failure signals are the critical enabler, not the model.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — Informs the structured FailureReflection artifact design in HID-174; contextual rather than actionable as a standalone issue.

source: arXiv:2606.30639 — Self-Evolving World Models for LLM Agent Planning
summary: Agents maintain executable code-based world models of their environment; models evolve as new observations arrive, allowing pre-commitment simulation of action consequences.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Plan stage is open-loop; a lightweight file-system world model could verify plan steps are internally consistent before implementation. Architecture is complex to integrate with CLI subprocess model.

source: arXiv:2605.02801 — RL for LLM-based Multi-Agent Systems through Orchestration Traces
summary: Formalizes orchestration decisions as a temporal interaction graph and applies RL (RLVR + GRPO) to optimize spawn/delegate/communicate/aggregate/stop decisions jointly.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Could learn when to skip or combine stages; requires significant execution trace data collection before RL training is feasible. Too early for AgentForge's current maturity.

source: arXiv:2606.31498 — Governance Gaps in Agent Interoperability Protocols
summary: Identifies what MCP/A2A/ACP cannot express: audit trails of delegation chains, mid-task authority revocation, cryptographic attestation of authorized scope.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — Relevant only if AgentForge delegates to third-party agents; not applicable to current single-orchestrator architecture.

source: Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 GA (April 2026) — AutoGen enters maintenance
summary: AutoGen is now maintenance-only; Microsoft Agent Framework 1.0 GA unifies AutoGen + Semantic Kernel for Python + .NET. AG2 community fork remains active for research.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge uses CLI subprocesses, not AutoGen's in-process orchestration; framework update noted but not applicable.

source: Google A2A Protocol v1.0.1 — Linux Foundation / AAIF (May 2026)
summary: Agent-to-agent protocol enabling capability discovery via Agent Cards, typed multi-turn performatives (propose/accept/reject/counter), and extension mechanism v1.0.1.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — AgentForge coordinates agents via CLI flags; A2A's capability discovery is only relevant when the agent pool grows to dynamically registered participants.

source: TianPan.co — Token Budget as Architecture Constraint (April 2026)
summary: Proposes surfacing token budget as part of the agent's own context; agent explicitly knows remaining budget and factors it into planning decisions (summarize earlier, escalate sooner).
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge has no cost visibility; opaque context-window exhaustion is a real failure mode. Scored lower than top 3 but worth revisiting when HID-175 is implemented.

source: Jim Fan / NVIDIA — Project GR00T and World Action Models (2026)
summary: Jim Fan's 2026 focus is embodied physical AI — humanoid foundation models, World Action Models trained on sensorized demonstrations. Physical robotics, not code agents.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — Embodied AI architecture; the world model concept is indirectly relevant but primary focus is robotics.

source: arXiv:2605.07935 — TraceFix: Repairing Agent Coordination Protocols with TLA+
summary: Uses TLA+ model checking to generate counterexamples for agent protocol failures, then LLM patches the protocol; verified patches pass the model checker.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — Formalizing AgentForge's state machine in TLA+ would surface unreachable/unrecoverable states; too engineering-heavy for a 1-2 sprint issue at current scale.

source: StreamMA — Streaming Partial Results in Multi-Agent Reasoning
summary: Pipelines multi-agent reasoning by streaming partial results; downstream agent begins processing before upstream completes; reduces latency and sometimes improves accuracy.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge blocks on full subprocess output; streaming plan output to implement stage could reduce wall-clock time. Requires significant changes to ProcessRunner stdout handling.

source: Temporal — Workflow Streams: Live Interactivity for Agents (2026)
summary: Temporal added workflow streams for surfacing intermediate agent state to external observers without halting execution; subscribers see live partial outputs.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — AgentForge has no observability into in-flight agent work; rolling buffer in ProcessRunner is partial solution but not subscriber-facing. Architectural change needed.
